We started 2025 with deliberative session in February followed by the Town Election on March 11, 2025. TOWN CLERK REPORT It comes with bittersweet emotion as I offer the residents of Exeter my final report as your Town Clerk. I will be retiring in May of 2026. I have given 20 years of service to the clerk’s office starting as an assistant to becoming the Town Clerk. I met all my goals I set for myself in 2012 when the residents of our town elected me as their Town Clerk. From remodeling, adding services, preservation of records and overall organization of the office, I have been blessed, and have loved every minute of it. But sadly, it is time for me to turn over the “wand”. Jennifer became Deputy in 2023 and has been training ever since to one day assume the role. Jennifer is compassionate, knowledgeable, and exuberant. She is the perfect person to fill my position. My hope is the residents of Exeter accept Jennifer with open arms knowing she is ready. We started 2025 with deliberative session in February followed by the Town Election on March 11, 2025. There was 17.6% voter participation with 2,296 ballots cast. Moderator, Kate Miller, announced the results at approximately 10:30 pm. In August, we accepted delivery of new ballot counting machines. We are trained and ready to assist voters. The machines will be used for the first time in the 2026 Town Election. The new machines will help Election Officials reconcile numbers at the end of the polling hours, which will aid in reporting to the State. In celebration of the 56th Annual Professional Municipal Clerks Week on May 5-9th, we decorated and wore attire coordinating with daily themes. The week is a time of celebration and reflection on the importance of the Clerk’s office. In 1984, President Ronald Reagan signed a proclamation that officially declared Municipal Clerks Week the first full week of May. In 1994 and 1996, President Bill Clinton also signed proclamations confirming Municipal Clerks Week as well as a yearly proclamation from the NH Governor’s Office. The week features a series of activities aimed at increasing the public’s awareness of Municipal Clerks and the vital services they provide for local government and the community. At the end of October, we had limited hours to attend the 100th Anniversary of the NH City & Town Clerks Association Conference at the Omni Mount Washington Resort. Attendees participated in educational classes, networking, and developing camaraderie with State Offices, legal counsel, and other state clerks. TOWN CLERK Being the HUB for questions and directions to anyone who enters or contacts the Municipal Center, the Town Clerk’s office is always very busy. Our office provides marriage licenses, vital records, election/voter information, and dog licenses. Dog renewals are due every year by April 30th, please remember to license your dog by this date to avoid paying fees and fines. The Town Clerk’s office licensed 7,756 dogs this past year. Our Animal Control Officer, along with members of the Derry Police Department have been a great help in contacting dog owners with late fees and having them license their dogs. We would like to thank the Police Department for their continued support in working with us to enforce this law. The Town Election this year showed a turnout of 3,218, or 16.9% of registered voters. This turnout represents an increase from the previous year. Erin Spencer was re-elected District #1 Councilor and Jack Webb was elected Councilor at Large. Jeffrey Strakalaitis was elected Trustee of the Trust Funds. David B Nelson was elected as Town Moderator. It is just as important to vote in your Town’s election as it is to vote in State and Presidential elections. The January Presidential Primary had a turnout of 8,998 voters. For every election we have absentee ballots for anyone that cannot make it to the polls on the day of the election. The absentee ballots are readily available and easy to obtain from the clerk. In closing I want to thank Sheila Bodenrader for the support to our office with her role as Clerk Designee to the Derry Town Council.
